## A collection, not a progression

- **One distinctive question**: a phenomenon, paradox, design decision, or research finding.
- **Visible reasoning**: concrete examples and, when useful, an explained mathematical derivation.
- **Critical perspective**: assumptions, limitations, counterexamples, and a clear distinction between theoretical results and empirical observations.
- **An experiment to take away**: a short calculation, prediction, or modification to extend the reading.

The four shelves are browsing aids, not stages to follow. Move directly from one question to another; the stories have no prerequisites.

## Edition status

The calendar lists the 24 topics planned for the 2026 edition. **One story out of 24 is currently available**; the other 23 remain in editorial preparation and may change if a topic proves repetitive, insufficiently sourced, or less valuable than an alternative.

The first story, about Zipf’s law, is published as a reading version open to feedback. It is the pilot for this model: one editorial door, one durable Deepen lesson, a dedicated exercise page, and links to related knowledge. Published pages will remain available year-round.

## Explore further

Each door is a narrative entry point to a permanent Deepen lesson. The lesson page carries the full content; the calendar does not duplicate the articles.

- [Browse the concept and resource map](learning-map.qmd) to navigate topics freely.
- [Explore Deepen](deepen.qmd) to find permanent lessons by domain.
- [Read the language-model overview](llm-overview.qmd) to place the main mechanisms in context.
- [Practice and experiment](exercises.qmd) to work through concepts from the main learning path.

These resources are optional extensions: none is required to read a calendar story.
